title: Anthropic&\#x27;s IPO roadshow details multi-chip Claude training across four chip families
summary: Anthropic opened its IPO roadshow on November 10, and the accompanying video contains previously unreleased detail on how the company runs its business; Simon Willison highlighted the "Approach to compute" section featuring co-founder Tom Brown. Brown says Anthropic now trains and serves Claude across all four major chip families — AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs and AMD GPUs — an early multi-chip bet he says many considered not worth the effort because each chip needs its own tailored software and inference stack. As a concrete example, he says Anthropic began working with AMD GPUs this year and that a system called Mythos got Claude running on AMD in three days with "basically no human intervention," porting or writing almost 100% of the kernels, where adding a new chip platform previously took dozens of engineers months. Brown also frames compute strategy around "compute multipliers" — total effective compute as physical capacity multiplied by discovered multipliers — and claims these stack and could grow faster as Anthropic approaches recursive self-improvement; these are company claims made in a promotional roadshow video, which has no official transcript \(Willison published one he extracted with MacWhisper\).
